subject: Post-call: Tool/function-calling integration patterns — SDK, auth, routing, embeddings
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finapps.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-15T15:04:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (tool/function-calling patterns)

Thanks again for taking the call today, Alex and Priya — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps focused on the integration patterns we discussed for tool/function calling and the follow-on architecture items: SDK setup, auth, routing, structured output, and embeddings/rerankers.

What we covered (high level):
- SDK + auth: Use Redwood SDK (server-side) with API key per-environment; for user-specific calls we suggested a short-lived proxy token pattern and optional signed JWTs if you want to attribute calls per-user.
- Tool definitions: Keep tool schemas small and explicit (name, input schema, output schema, error schema). Prefer typed JSON schema for structured output and validation.
- Tool choice + orchestration: Decide per-utterance whether to call a single tool or fan-out to parallel tools (e.g., lookup + enrichment). We'll recommend coordinator logic in your backend that calls tools in parallel and merges results.
- Error handling: Use idempotent tool design, explicit retry/backoff for transient failures, and graceful fallback to a safe default or the base model for best-effort responses.
- Embeddings & rerankers: Use an embeddings index for candidate retrieval, then use a lightweight reranker model (or a tuned prompt on the LLM) to rank. Consider hybrid: vector similarity for recall, reranker for precision.

Deliverables I attached: redwood-tool-calling-patterns.pdf (patterns + examples), a sample JSON schema for tool definitions, and a checklist for auth/keys.

Open items / actions for FinApps:
1) Confirm target qps and 95th percentile latency SLO for user-facing flows (helps us size batch/replica configs).
2) Share a short list of the first 3 tool types you want to expose (examples: payments-lookup, customer-profile, transaction-normalizer).
3) Any data residency / retention constraints we should plan for.

Next steps we propose:
- Technical deep-dive with your infra and backend engineers (30–45m) — propose Thu 1/21 or Mon 1/25.
- We’ll send a short demo repo with SDK snippets and a sample tool definition.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate scheduling once you confirm preferred slot.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (tool/function-calling patterns)

Thanks Marissa — super helpful summary. Quick answers:
- Latency SLO: 200ms p95 for simple lookups, 800ms p95 for composition flows that touch multiple tools. Expected peak qps for the pilot: ~120 qps.
- Initial tool list: customer-profile (lookup by email/id), transaction-normalizer (parse raw bank descriptions), balance-lookup (real-time).
- Data residency: US only for now. Retention: log-level telemetry for 90 days; no raw PII persisted in our index (we can token-hash/anonymize).

Thu 1/21 10:00 PT works for the deep-dive — please send an invite and any pre-reads you want the eng team to review. Also can you include an example of the parallel tool fan-out you mentioned? That will help our architects.

— Alex

Hi Alex — quick note from an engineering perspective before the deep-dive:
- Parallel fan-out pattern (example): client triggers a coordinator service -> coordinator issues parallel HTTP calls to tools A/B/C with a 250ms per-call deadline -> responses are merged via deterministic merger (timestamp + source priority) -> reranker invoked if >1 candidate. If any tool times out, we attach an error code and continue with remaining results.
- SDK setup: we recommend using Redwood server SDK on your backend (Node/Go). Keep tool callers server-side to protect API keys and run the coordinator there. For user attribution, we can mint short-lived tokens via your auth service (signed JWTs) so we can preserve per-user telemetry without exposing long-lived keys.
- Structured output: please use our recommended output envelope: {"status":"ok|error","result":<typed-json> ,"meta":{"tool":"name","latency_ms":123}} — this makes retries and merges easier.

I'll bring a short slide with pseudo-code and a sample coordinator flow to the call. Anything else you want covered?

— Ethan

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (tech deep-dive prep)

Great questions — quick answers and what we'll bring to the call:
- Fallback policy example: primary: tool call -> if tool times out or returns transient 5xx, retry once with exponential backoff (100ms -> 300ms). If still failing, mark tool as degraded and: a) return best-effort result from remaining tools or b) return structured error to client with a suggested human-readable message. We ship a policy template you can adopt.
- Embeddings & sensitive fields: recommended workflow: 1) tokenize/hash sensitive identifiers (PII) before indexing, 2) store only vector + non-identifying metadata, 3) use encryption-at-rest (customer-managed keys if required), and 4) enforce a TTL on vectors if you need retention limits. We'll share a short code snippet for client-side token hashing and for server-side anonymization.

Attached are two short snippets in the PDF and a link to the docs: https://redwood-inference.app/docs/tool-calling-patterns. For the deep-dive Thu 1/21 10:00 PT, I'll send a calendar invite and a 4-slide pre-read that highlights: coordinator pseudo-code, SDK usage, auth token flow, and sample tool definitions.

Would you like us to include a short checklist for compliance (KMS, logging, audit) in the pre-read?

Best,
